title: Service Desk – Diagnostics-First Support Platform & In-App Vue Widget
subtitle: Multi-tenant helpdesk unifying a native Vue in-app widget, IMAP email and public web forms into one agent inbox, shipped as reusable NPM packages for the company suite and as a standalone web app.
description: Delivered a diagnostics-first support platform unifying 3 intake channels in one agent inbox, shipped as reusable NPM packages for the company suite plus a standalone web app, via database-driven app routing and server-side PII redaction.
classification: 🔒 Proprietary Enterprise IP · Proficient Information Systems

contribution.label: Solo Engineer & Product Owner · Proficient Information Systems
contribution.headline: Planned, validated with the client, and delivered the Service Desk hub, reusable NPM packages, native Vue in-app widget and standalone web app as the only engineer, working from architecture direction set by the CEO and company architect.
scope: Product planning and requirements verification with the client, then end-to-end implementation
Reusable NPM package components (@itc/service-desk) integrated into the company suite, plus a standalone web app separate from the suite

database: MySQL (streams, apps registry, mailboxes, RBAC, forms)

keyDecisions.challenge: Hardcoded .env stream mapping forced a deploy for every new Vue app.
keyDecisions.decision: Moved routing into a support_widget_apps table (app_id, support_stream_id, allowed_origins, is_active) with a widget-only middleware resolving the stream per request.
keyDecisions.outcome: Apps register through /service-desk/apps with zero code deploys; unregistered app_id submissions are rejected with 400.

keyDecisions.challenge: New widget routing must never break existing email and form intake.
keyDecisions.decision: Scoped the middleware strictly to POST /api/v1/support/me/tickets so SupportEmailIngressService (IMAP) and public form controllers keep native mailbox/form stream mappings.
keyDecisions.outcome: Three channels coexist in one inbox; validated end to end across widget, email and form lifecycles.

keyDecisions.challenge: 'Cannot reproduce' tickets from missing client state.
keyDecisions.decision: Packaged a versioned diagnostics pack (schema_version 1): route metadata, viewport, locale, tenant, a ring-buffer of the last 20 Axios calls with request_id, and trapped window.onerror, unhandled rejections and Vue errors.
keyDecisions.outcome: Every in-app ticket arrives with reproducible context and an isolated last_failed_api.

keyDecisions.challenge: Diagnostics can leak credentials and PII into tickets.
keyDecisions.decision: Enforced server-side sanitization: drop unmapped keys, cap payload size, redact Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie and API keys before persisting as support.context and diagnostics.json.
keyDecisions.outcome: Debug context without storing secrets in the ticket store.

keyDecisions.challenge: Support had to work inside the company suite and also as an independent product, without duplicating UI code.
keyDecisions.decision: Packaged the agent console and in-app widget as reusable NPM components (@itc/service-desk) consumed by the suite, and built a standalone web app on the same packages.
keyDecisions.outcome: One shared codebase serves both the integrated suite experience and the standalone product; new host apps embed support by installing the package.

keyDecisions.challenge: Variable custom ticket fields vs strict relational config.
keyDecisions.decision: Dual-database: MongoDB for flexible ticket documents and threads, MySQL for streams, apps, mailboxes, forms and RBAC.
keyDecisions.outcome: Schema flexibility for custom attributes with relational integrity for administration.

keyDecisions.decision: Dual-lane threading: public replies trigger sanitized SMTP, private notes stay internal within one chronological thread.
keyDecisions.outcome: Zero accidental exposure of internal notes to customers.

securityReliability: Sanctum session auth plus tenant-isolation middleware verifying membership and permissions on every API call.
Origin allow-list (allowed_origins) and is_active flag per registered app; 400 for unregistered app_id.
Server-side payload scrubbing and header redaction for diagnostics packs.
Encrypted app secrets and mailbox credentials; never exposed in API responses.
Anti-spam on public forms: double opt-in, honeypot, IP rate limits, reCAPTCHA.
Isolated queue workers separating IMAP polling from outbound notifications.

MVP 4: two-way webhook sync with Jira, Linear and GitHub; FRT and resolution dashboards; CSAT automation; integration failure alerts.
